caseno: Appeal From Appellate Decree No. 88 of 1974
lawyer:
Ahmed Sobhan with Md. Fazlul Karim and Md. Ruhul Amin---------For the Appellant. 
Md. Hazrat Ali----------For Respondent No. 1
parties:
Jahangirnagar Muslim University----------- Petitioner.
Vs.
Savor Dairy Farm -------- Opp. Party.
full_judgment:
The Agricultural Department, Government of East Pakistan by its memo No. XI/Misc. 46/63/610 dated 14. 12. 63 addressed to the Director of Livestock Services, East Pakistan, Dacca approved the construction of a prayer hall within the Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm, Savar on an area of 150 ft. x 70 ft. x land subject to the condition that no costs for the prayer hall shall be met from provisions for the scheme for the Savar Dairy Farm or from the Government and that the prayer hall will not hamper the activities of the Farm in any way at present or in future. The Director of Livestock Services, East Pakistan, forwarded a copy of the said letter to the Manager, Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm, Savar, who directed the Chairman of the Savar Dairy Firm Mosque Committee to ask the Secretary of the Mosque Committee to start the construction work by his letter dated 26.1.1964. The Mosque Committee started construction with the subscription of the members of the public. For the purpose of paying monthly salary of the Imam and Khadim of the Mosque, the Mosque Committee permitted Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia to construct kutcha shop rooms at their own expenses within the mosque land facing Dacca-Aricha Road on condition that they will pay rent at Rs. 10/- per month to the Mosque Committee. Accordingly said Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia constructed two kutcha shop rooms within the mosque land in 1964 and established grocery shops. Buildings of the Jahangirnagar Muslim University are being constructed on the western side of the Dacca Aricha Road on the land owned and possessed by the Savar Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm. The Manager of the Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm, Savar in his memo No. 2-U325(2) dated 7.2.69 informed Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia that the entire farm land of the western side of the Dacca Aricha road has been handed over to the Education Department for the Jahangirnagar Muslim University and asked them to remove their structures and shops. The Project Director, Jahangirnagar Muslim University by his Memo No. PD/JMU/ LA-3/68/657 dated 24.6.69 asked Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia to vacate the place and remove their shops and other belongings within seven days of the issue of the said order. The alleged making over of the land of the mosque including the two shops of Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia to the University had been done beyond the knowledge of the Mosque Committee after the Mosque Committee came to possess the land in question and after the pucca mosque was constructed on the land with public subscription. The defendant No. 1 (Government of East Pakistan) had no right to interfere with the possession of the mosque and its compound and had no authority to hand over the same to the Jahangirnagar Muslim University. As the handing over of the prayer hall and its land to the Education Department of the Government of East, Pakistan is void and without jurisdiction, the aforesaid orders dated 7.2.69 passed by the Manager, Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm Savar and the Project Director, Jahangirnagar Muslim University respectively are also illegal and void and not binding on the plaintiff and its tenants. 

 6. Mr. Ahmad, Sobhan, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant University argues that the plaintiff Chairman of the so-called Savar Dairy Farm Mosque committee has no locus standi to file the suit, that the courts below erred in law in holding without any evidence that the Government made donation or gift of the suit land to the plaintiff-Respondent for construction of a prayer hall, that the courts below erred in law in holding that the Mosque Committee (Plaintiff) had acquired valid right, title and interest in the suit property by virtue of any allotment from the Department concerned of the Government, that the findings of the courts below are based on total miconception of law and facts and misconstruction of documents and that on these grounds the judgments and decree passed by the courts below should be set aside. He further argued that the Mosque Committee has no existence in the eye of law and that Government gave no permission to anyone to construct any shop in the suit premises for outsiders. 

 7. It appears from the Government of East Pakistan (Agricultural Deptt.) Memo No. XI/Misc. 46/63/610 dated 14-12-63 that the Agricultural Department of the Government of East Pakistan permitted the Director of Livestocks Services, East Pakistan to construct a prayer hall within the Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm, Savar on an area of 150' x 70' lof land. But at no stage they permitted Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia or the plaintiff Chairman to make construction of any shop whatsoever in the compound. The Courts below have not at all considered the contents of the impugned letters dated 7-2-69 and 24-6-69 issued by the Manager, Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm, Savar and the Project Director, Jahangirnagar Muslim University respectively upon Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia. No right, title, possession or any interest in the suit land at any stage was transferred by the Government to the Mosque Committee and the structures erected by Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia in the compound of the prayer hall are unauthorised. The Agricultural Department of the Government had every right to transfer the suit land to the Education Department for the Jahangirnagar Muslim University and the appellant Jahangirnagar Muslim University is not at all interfering in any manner with the prayer hall. As the right, title and interest: in the suit land remain vested in the Government, the handing over of the suit land by the Agriculture Department to the Education Department for the Jahangirnagar University was valid and legal. Manager, Dairy and Cattle Improvement Farm, Savar by his letter dated 7-2-69 asked Md. Khalilur Raman and Md. Chand Mia to vacate the premises. Similarly the Project Director, Jahangirnagar Muslim University by his letter dated 24-6-69 asked Md. Khalilur Rahman and Md. Chand Mia to vacate the suit premises. No illegality at all has been committed by these orders. The plaintiff has no locus standi to file the suit. There is no evidence to show that the Government made donation or gift of the suit land to the plaintiff. There is also no evidence to show that the Mosque Committee (plaintiff) had acquired any valid right, title or interest in the suit land or right to construct or allow anyone to construct any shop in the suit land. In that view of the matter the judgments and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and the learned Munsif cannot be sustained and must be set aside. 

 8. Mr. Md. Hazrat Ali, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-Respondent argued that this Court has no jurisdiction to interfere with the concurrent findings of facts of the Courts below. In this connection the decisions in the cases of Khandker Mohiuddin Vs. Mohiuddin Ahmad 28 D.L.R. (App. Div.) 90, Fateh Chand Vs. Kishen Kunwar 39 I.A. 247, Dame,sa Vs. Ahdus Samad 46 I.A. 140 and Sheikh Rahmat Elahi Vs. Mohammad Hayat Khan and others, A.I.R. 1943 (P.C.) 208 may be referred to. In the case of Khandkor Mohiuddin Moin Ahmed 28 DLR (App. Div.) 98 their Lordships of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh observed, : 

 9. It is well settled that a second appeal is not competent against findings of facts based on some evidence. This Court can any interfere in second appeal on the ground of law or defect in procedure. In this connection it is worth-while to refer to the decision in the case of Fateh Chand Vs. Kishen Kunwar 39 I.A. 247 wherein their Lordships of the Privy Council observed: 

 "The judges of the High Court rightly overruled the objection that they were bound to accept as correct the findings of the Subordinate Judge that the plaintiffs were the proprietors of the lands to which this suit referred. That finding of the Subordinate Judge was the result of his having misconstrued the Wajibul Arz. The construction of documents is a question of law which the judges in second appeal are not by Ss. 584 and 585 (now sec. 100) of the Code of Civil Procedure precluded from considering by any finding of a lower appellate Court based upon such documents. The Subordinate Judge arrived at his findings by inferences drawn upon an incorrect construction of Wajibul Arz and the judges in second appeal consequently were not bound by his finding that the plaintiffs were the proprietors of the lands." 

 10. In the case of Sheikh Rahmat Elahi Vs. Mohammad Hayat Khan and others, A.I.R. 1943 (P.C.) 208 their Lordships of the Privy Council observed: 

 "Their Lordships had occasion to point out in Damusa Vs:Abdus Samad 46 I.A. 140 that where the Courts below had misconceived the real question of fact they had to try, there was an error of law on which a second appeal lay; and their Lordships can see no difference in principle between a failure to appreciate and determine the real question of fact to be tried and a failure to appreciate and determine a question of fact which vitally affects the issue stated in the case. In either case failure is a failure in the duty imposed by law upon the Court and the question whether there has been such a failure must in their Lordships opinion be a question of law." 

 11. So incorrect construction of a material document is an error of law. Where the Courts below misconceive the real question of fact to be tried, it is an error of law. A failure to appreciate and determine a question of fact which affects the issues stated in the case is an error of law. 

 12. In this case it has been shown that the Courts below misconstrued the documents filed by the plaintiff-Respondent in support of his claim and on such incorrect construction of the documents erroneously held that the Government made donation or gift of the suit land to the plaintiff for construction of a prayer Hall and that the Mosque Committee (plaintiff) had acquired any valid right, title and interest in the suit property by virtue of any allotment from any Department of the Government or had any right to construct or allow anyone to construct shops in the suit land. These are errors of law and the judgments and decree of the Courts below being based on these illegal findings must be set aside. As the plaintiff has no right, title or interest in the suit land or any right to construct or allow anyone to construct shops on the suit land and let it out to anyone, his suit must be dismissed.
